title: Normal Stein factor and its algebraic constant field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $f:T\to B$ be a proper dominant morphism of integral schemes of finite type over $k$. Suppose $T$ is normal, meaning that all its local rings are integrally closed domains. Put $E=k(T)$ and $F=k(B)$ with the inclusion induced by $f$. There is a factorization $T\xrightarrow{g}B_0\xrightarrow{q}B$ in which $q$ is finite and dominant, $B_0$ is normal integral of finite type over $k$, and $g$ is proper with geometrically connected fibres. It has the specified construction $B_0=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_B(f_*\mathcal O_T)$: for an affine open $V\subseteq B$, $q^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(f^{-1}V,\mathcal O_T)$, and $g$ on $f^{-1}V$ is the morphism induced by evaluation of these sections. Inside $E$ its function field is
$$k(B_0)=\{a\in E:a\text{ is algebraic over }F\}.$$
In particular this field is finite over $F$ and is algebraically closed in $E$. Schemes, integrality, properness, finite type and finite morphisms use [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Function fields, affine spectra, geometric connectedness and relative algebraic closure use [def-sc-function-field], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the two structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Thus $T$ and $B$ are Noetherian. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-noetherian-normal-stein-model] hold; it supplies the normal integral $B_0$, finite dominant $q$, dominant proper $g$ with geometrically connected fibres, and exactly the relative-spectrum charts and evaluation maps required here.

Choose a finite affine cover $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $B$ with each $A_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The charts of step 1 give $q^{-1}V_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, with $R_i$ finite over $A_i$. A finite list of $A_i$-module generators of $R_i$, together with $k$-algebra generators of $A_i$, generates $R_i$ as a $k$-algebra. These finitely many affine charts cover $B_0$, proving that $B_0$ is of finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 03H0; finite-module generators give the elementary finite-type consequence

proof.text: Fix a nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq B$ and put $U=f^{-1}V$, $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_T)$. Dominance makes $U$ nonempty and $U\to V$ dominant; its local rings are those of $T$, so $U$ is normal integral. Step 1 gives $R$ finite over $A$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-sections-algebraic-constants] to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $F=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and $k(B_0)=\operatorname{Frac}R$. Also $k(U)=E$, since restriction to a nonempty open preserves the generic point and its local ring. The evaluation map in step 1 identifies the embedding of $k(B_0)$ into $E$ with the fraction-field embedding of $R\subseteq E$. Thus the cited constant-field theorem gives the required equality, finiteness over $F$, and algebraic closedness in $E$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_normal_stein_constant_field (k : Type u) [Field k] {T B : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral T] [IsIntegral B] (t : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (b : B ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType t] [QuasiCompact t] [LocallyOfFiniteType b] [QuasiCompact b] (f : T ⟶ B) [IsProper f] [IsDominant f] (hf : f ≫ b = t) (hT : ∀ x : T, IsDomain (T.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (T.presheaf.stalk x)) : ∃ (B₀ : Scheme.{u}) (q : B₀ ⟶ B) (g : T ⟶ B₀), ∃ (_ : IsIntegral B₀) (_ : IsDominant q) (_ : IsDominant g), g ≫ q = f ∧ IsFinite q ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (q ≫ b) ∧ QuasiCompact (q ≫ b) ∧ (∀ x : B₀, IsDomain (B₀.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (B₀.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ IsProper g ∧ GeometricallyConnected g ∧ (∀ V : B.Opens, IsAffineOpen V → IsIso (g.app (q ⁻¹ᵁ V))) ∧ Set.range (@algebraMap B₀.functionField T.functionField _ _ (g.dominantFunctionFieldAlgebra)) = (↑(@algebraicClosure B.functionField T.functionField _ _ (f.dominantFunctionFieldAlgebra)) : Set T.functionField) ∧ (@algebraMap B.functionField B₀.functionField _ _ (q.dominantFunctionFieldAlgebra)).Finite ∧ @algebraicClosure B₀.functionField T.functionField _ _ (g.dominantFunctionFieldAlgebra) = ⊥
